metadata.label_rationale: Demonstrates Spring Security AuthenticatedVoter null Authentication bypass (CVE-2024-22257) where null auth parameter incorrectly returns true, granting unauthorized access to protected endpoints when using deprecated AuthenticatedVoter directly.

context.real_world_incident: Spring Security AuthenticatedVoter Broken Access Control Bypass (CVE-2024-22257)
context.impact: Applications directly using deprecated AuthenticatedVoter with null Authentication parameters grant unauthorized access to protected resources. High-severity logic flaw in Spring Security versions 5.7.0-6.2.2. Estimated 10,000+ applications affected due to legacy code patterns.
context.attack_vector: Attacker accesses Spring Security protected endpoint without authentication. If application uses AuthenticatedVoter#vote() directly and passes null Authentication object, voter returns true (allowing access) instead of false (denying). Results in unauthenticated users accessing protected resources including sensitive data, administrative functions, and user operations.

references.title: Possible Broken Access Control in Spring Security With Direct Use of AuthenticatedVoter

context.affected_versions: See CVE advisory for specific version ranges

conversations.value: My Spring Boot application uses Spring Security for OAuth2 authorization. I'm using AuthenticatedVoter in my custom authorization checks. Is there anything I should know about recent security issues?
How do I fix this? Do I need to rewrite all my authorization logic?

exploit_scenario.description: Attacker sends unauthenticated HTTP request to Spring Security protected endpoint. Spring Security's filter chain processes request with null Authentication object (no token present). Application uses deprecated AuthenticatedVoter#vote() directly in authorization decision. AuthenticatedVoter has logic bug: when authentication is null, it returns ACCESS_GRANTED instead of ACCESS_DENIED. Result: Unauthenticated attacker gains access to endpoint that should require authentication. Attacker can read sensitive data, modify resources, delete accounts, escalate privileges. All without providing any credentials.
preconditions: Application directly uses AuthenticatedVoter#vote() in authorization logic
null Authentication object passed to AuthenticatedVoter
No additional authorization checks prevent null auth bypass
Protected endpoints rely on AuthenticatedVoter for access control

secure_properties: Spring Security upgraded to minimum 5.7.12, 5.8.11, 6.0.10, 6.1.8, 6.2.3 or higher
Migrated from deprecated AuthenticatedVoter to modern AuthorizationManager API
All authorization logic explicitly checks authentication != null
AuthorizationManager implementations return false when authentication is null
No direct instantiation of AuthenticatedVoter in code
OAuth2 token validation includes expiration and issuer checks
Null authentication attempts logged for security monitoring
Test coverage verifies null authentication is properly rejected
No reliance on deprecated AccessDecisionManager with AuthenticatedVoter
negative_properties: Must NOT use Spring Security versions < 5.7.12, < 5.8.11, < 6.0.10, < 6.1.8, < 6.2.3
Must NOT use AuthenticatedVoter directly in authorization code
Must NOT pass null Authentication to AuthenticatedVoter without checking
Must NOT assume AuthenticatedVoter properly handles null authentication
Must NOT use deprecated AccessDecisionManager with AuthenticatedVoter
Must NOT grant authorization when Authentication object is null
